correctness.rationale: The reduction to all possible five-element noncommutative nilpotent multiplication types, a 63-digraph exhaustive finite-duality test, and the two-generator/two-output case together prove the exact nine and exclude all smaller orders. An independent odd-cycle obstruction for the acyclic path provides a conceptual nonfinite-duality witness. The enumerator reproduces the 15 three-vertex graph types, four finitely based noncommutative types, eight nonfinitely based noncommutative graph types, and exactly one additional two-output class. The index-four exhaustive table test covers 1,296 filtration-compatible table candidates and all eight associative noncommutative survivors, each with a nonzero pure cube. This proof depends explicitly on already published finite-duality and full-power-semiring theorems; no finite experiment is misrepresented as an infinite nonfinite-basis proof.

value.rationale: The smallest-cardinality boundary and all exact isomorphism classes of noncommutative nilpotent semigroups with nonfinitely based full power semirings give a canonical structural cutoff at order five, separating previously known order-four negative commutative cases and order-four positive noncommutative cases. The eight graph supports and ninth two-output type make a natural complete classification of an invariant directly motivated by the October 2026 general finite-basis theorem; in particular, the path case shows directed cycles are not required. Exact small-order classification and minimality have utility for testing future structural criteria, not merely a random finite instance.
